Finite check replay specification: form M on the listed sign triples and residues; compute powers through 24 and use Newton identities, RESULT.md lines 49–53, for the full integer polynomial. For a separate finite cross-check, enumerate all 3ⁿ words for n=3–10 and test adjacency and the richness definition directly.
correctness.rationale: For a proper coloring a rich edge occurs exactly at equality of the two incident sign increments around its color. Thus the rich-neighbor condition at i is equality of the two signs on the left or equality of the two on the right. Successive sign triples enforce every such test, and residue closure enforces sum of all signs equal to zero modulo three. For each admissible indexed sign word there are exactly three starting residues, just as there are three initial named colors. A walk is indexed by its starting time, not taken modulo rotation. This verifies the trace count including n=3. Independently constructed integer matrices reproduced the stated polynomial and traces through power 24; direct color tests matched n=3–10 and independent sign-word tests matched through n=18. In the sign graph one can reach a constant triple by repeating the terminal sign, reach either constant triple, and then build any target triple. The four-step −+++ return at +++ changes residue by 2, establishing residue adjustment. The length-three and length-five returns with modular sum zero certify primitivity. As an independent spectral check, for x=1[a≠b], y=1[b≠c] the transition on these bits is (x,y)→(y,z) with xz=0. The vector f(x)f(y) with f(0)=φ, f(1)=1 lifts to a strictly positive φ-eigenvector of M. By primitivity φ is simple and strictly dominant, so the power trace has leading coefficient one and no periodic modulation. The total proper count is the trace of the three-color off-diagonal adjacency matrix, 2ⁿ+2(−1)ⁿ.
residual_risks: Finite integer checks certify only the displayed factorization and finite counts; the trace bijection and primitivity proof control the full sequence. The result is for named three-color assignments on a labeled cycle, not graphs modulo automorphisms or unrestricted palettes.

The closest same-property cycle literature gives existence/chromatic index and the exceptions C₄ and C₇, not the count. Related exact enumerations for ladders and complete bipartite graphs use other graphs and palettes. No inspected primary statement or indexed theorem implies the displayed trace count or determinant. This does not assert exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: The graph family and named palette are natural: three is the feasibility threshold on all but two cycle lengths in the earlier colorability result. Counting all such colorings answers how frequent the feasible property is within proper colorings, including the exact growth constant, leading coefficient, and exponential sparsity. The distance-two local rule plus cyclic residue constraint supply an all-length classification, not small-case recomputation or a restatement of existence. The exact spectral formula is a usable invariant for later enumeration and asymptotics.
residual_risks: No conclusion for wider palettes, unlabeled cycles, or general degree-two subgraphs beyond what follows directly for disjoint labeled cycles.
